precepts.text: God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. And Adam begat a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth. Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone's not made in God's image. Cain was not made in God's image; Seth was; Abel was. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he wasn't God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.
precepts.point: The earth also was corrupt before God: because the sons of God started to mingle with the daughters of men, Cain's children. Cain gained dominion on the earth. And the earth was filled with violence: just like Cain was violent. Is the earth full of violence today? Yes. The end of all flesh is come before me; behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

precepts.text: Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in the creation. Adam had his righteous child, Seth, and Noah had his righteous child, Shem, and out of Shem's line came us.
precepts.point: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

precepts.text: Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner. Look upon all the works of the most High, and there are two and two, one against another. There's always a good side and a bad side. You had a righteous Enoch and you had a wicked one.
precepts.point: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

precepts.text: This is Cain's kids: unto Enoch was born Irad, and Mehujael begat Methusael, and Methusael begat Lamech. So Cain had a son named Enoch, one named Methusael, and one named Lamech. Two is always: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.
precepts.point: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

precepts.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness. That was the point: everybody is not in God's image.
precepts.point: Everybody came from Adam, but everybody is not a child of God. Satan's kids come from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Why is it written like that? Seth was in Adam's likeness, after Adam's image. It never says that about Cain. John said Cain “was of that wicked one”: Cain was in the image of Satan, not in the image of Adam.

Go back to the beginning: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That was the point. God's image was given to man, and that image carried down to Seth, but everybody is not in God's image.

Everybody came from Adam, yes, but Satan's kids came from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage. Coming from Adam does not make someone a child of God. The image and likeness went through Seth, and that is the line to follow through Genesis.

precepts.text: The Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and man became a living soul. That was Adam. Adam was in God's image; Seth was in the image of Adam, who was in the image of God.
precepts.point: Everybody came from Adam, but everybody is not a child of God. Satan's kids come from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” That was Adam. God made Adam in his own image and breathed the breath of life into him.

Read Genesis 5:3 again with that in mind: Adam “begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Seth was in the image of Adam, and Adam was in the image of God. So Seth carried God's image.

Cain was not in the image of God. He was not in Adam's image, and he was not in God's image; he was of that wicked one. That is why everybody is not a child of God, and why Cain's line and Seth's line have to be read differently. All of this was playing out in the city Cain built, named Enoch after his son.

precepts.text: Adam begat a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth. Cain is never said to be in Adam's image.
precepts.point: Cain's line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Don’t you see something wrong there? Abel was already dead, and Cain was still alive. So why does it never say that Cain was in Adam’s image?

Go back to the making of Adam: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle”. Adam, the black man, was made in the image of God. Adam and Eve had Cain and Abel; Cain killed Abel, because God had told him that if he did not do well, sin lay at the door and Satan would rule over him.

Then, when it names the son born “in his own likeness, after his image”, it names Seth, not Cain. People say everybody is in the image of God. No: Cain was not in the image of God, and he is never said to be in Adam’s image.

So whose image was Cain in? John answers it: Cain “was of that wicked one”. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of Satan. That is why the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are two different seeds, and why Seth’s line, the line that returns as Jacob, is the one that carries Adam’s image.

precepts.text: Adam knew Eve his wife, and she bare Cain.
precepts.point: The earth has not yet been subdued, and that waits for the kingdom.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Why was Adam told to subdue the earth? Because he lost it. Satan says all the power and glory of this earth was given to him, and he can give it to whoever he wants. Adam lost rulership of the earth, so now he has to come and subdue it again, and kill Satan.

“And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Cain was not created in Adam's image. She said she got a man, and we keep reading about the children of men; his very name tells you he was not created in Adam's image or after his likeness. “And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Cain killed Abel. Abel was righteous and Cain was wicked, and Abel was supposed to be the righteous child created in Adam's image.

So what did the Lord do? Genesis 4 and 5 are the replenishing of the earth, filling it again with the righteous seed, his sons. Genesis 2 goes into Adam's rulership, Genesis 2 and 3 are the same as Ezekiel 31, Adam's rule and his fall, and Genesis 4 and 5 are Adam and Eve replenishing the earth after the fall.

Genesis 5: “This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam”. Adam means from the ground. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Now the sons of God, the children above, start being sent down to the earth and born through Adam and his descendants. The twelve tribes are born into the earth through him. Seth's whole lineage is the sons of God, Israel, born in the image of God. Cain was not.

The command to replenish the earth and subdue it is not finished. The earth has not yet been subdued, and that waits for the kingdom.

precepts.text: The man made in our image, created he him, is the first Adam; male and female created he them is the other people.
precepts.point: When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.” Then: “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Two things are said there, and Genesis 5 says them the same way: “in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them.”

The man made in our image, “created he him”, is the first Adam, made in the likeness of God, a direct descendant of the Most High. “Male and female created he them” is the other people: they were not that Adam. When the Most High creates a fish He does not create only a salmon; there is mackerel and tuna and all types of fish. In the same way, He created Adam and He created the other people, and called their name Adam in the day when they were created.

precepts.text: Christ's lineage on his mother's side runs back through Seth to Adam, the son of God.
precepts.point: When Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
Christ’s lineage on his mother’s side runs straight back through this book of the generations of Adam: “Which was the son of Cainan, which was the son of Arphaxad, which was the son of Sem, which was the son of Noe, which was the son of Lamech, Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan, Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.”

Adam was the son of God, and chapter 5 is his direct lineage. That lineage is the sons of God of chapter 6, and through Shem it ties the Israelites directly to the line of Adam. That is why, when Christ said, Ye are gods, He was saying we come from that line of Adam, the son of God.

precepts.text: Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven; that is what it means that God took Enoch.
precepts.point: Enoch walked with God and was not: the Most High took him up, and Enoch did not taste death, the same way Elijah did not taste death.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
Elijah did not taste death, and neither did Enoch. Elijah told Elisha, “if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee”; and as they still went on and talked, “there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.”

That is what it means that God took Enoch. “Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.” The Most High took him up, the same way Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven.

precepts.text: Christ was taken up and received in a cloud; taken up means received by the Most High.
precepts.point: Enoch walked with God and was not: the Most High took him up, and Enoch did not taste death, the same way Elijah did not taste death.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
“And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” Christ was taken up and received in a cloud. Taken up means received by the Most High.

So “God took him” is Enoch being taken up and received the same way. He walked with God, and he was not, because the Most High took him up, as Elijah was taken and as Christ was taken.
